mappings.note: The bean plant's life cycle stage by stage. Explaining a process, LO-110.
Compare and contrast the mosquito and frog life cycles. An explicit differentiation of two organisms' development, LO-106.
Death within the life cycle -- all activity ceasing despite resources. Explaining a life process, LO-110.
Every change a frog passes through from spawn to adult. Explaining a developmental process, LO-110.
How gravity governs root and shoot direction, whatever the plant's orientation. A growth pattern related to its cause, LO-109; LO-110 would lose the causal emphasis the item requires.
Respiration in animals and plants, how it is similar and how it DIFFERS. The differentiation is half the item, LO-106.
Why movement alone misleads when sorting living from non-living -- cars move, plants largely do not. Requires the distinction to rest on the full property set, LO-106.
How the life cycle secures continuity of the species in plants and animals. Explaining a process, LO-110.
Avadhi's seeds did not germinate despite sunlight. LO-108 for diagnosing the missing condition and fixing the set-up, LO-109 for part (ii), which asks why water matters and light does not.
Folding leaves and insect-trapping hairs: LO-110 for the plant movements themselves, LO-106 for part (iii), which asks whether these count as movement in the animal sense.
Community measures against mosquito breeding. LO-115 for the protective action -- draining water, covering containers -- and LO-109 for part (ii), which asks how the kerosene film kills.
Avadhi's outgrown dress shows growth, and part (ii) asks whether non-living things grow. The living/non-living differentiation is what the item turns on, LO-106.
Pond observations named as spawn and tadpoles (LO-105), then part (iii) asks how the habitat changes from those stages to the adult (LO-106).
